correctness.rationale: On the 13-point and 13-line plane of order three, total domination forces each selected side to be a blocker/cover of cardinality at least four. Four-point blockers are lines; a four-point side requires at least eight opposite-side selected vertices for location. Incidence pair-counting forces every five-point blocker to be one line plus an exterior point, and dually every five-line cover to be a pencil plus one line. Comparing all open-neighborhood signatures proves precisely the stated parameters. The unique full line and pencil are invariant under any one-vertex exchange; independent binary choices of the remaining point and line give exactly 468 components, each C4. Python independently exhausts all 4..6 cardinality splits of combined size at most ten and confirms 1872 optima and adjacency, while independently implemented C++ bitmask enumeration confirms the same counts and components. Proof and actual source files were reconstructed and checked; no failed computation is used as a proof of impossibility.

value.rationale: The unique order-three finite projective plane, with its canonical 26-vertex incidence graph, is the first step beyond the Fano plane. Exact locating-total domination is a natural sensor-location invariant with both coverage and distinction constraints, not a selected arbitrary subset count. The minimum ten represents a two-vertex penalty over ordinary total domination eight; the complete 1872-state classification has a clean nonincident-flag parameterization, and the 468 disjoint squares expose a sharp structural failure of optimum-preserving mobility despite each state admitting two moves. These exact properties neither follow from scalar metric dimension eight nor ordinary domination six and are useful as concrete equality/reconfiguration benchmarks. The finite nature is not itself treated as evidence of value.
